newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA SHARES END LOWER, SNAP OUT OF EIGHT-DAY RISE.
newsitem.headline: MANILA SHARES END LOWER, SNAP OUT OF EIGHT-DAY RISE.

text.p: Philippine stocks paused for a breather on Thursday after climbing for eight straight sessions as investors cashed in gains made in blue chips, traders said.

"It's too good to be true for the run-up to be sustained. This is a technical correction given the fact that volumes in all except one of the eight sessions were relatively thin," Jun Trinidad, research head at DBS Securities Phils Inc, said.
The main index closed 24.78 points lower, or 0.92 percent, at 2,670.01 points.
Turnover was thin at 1.9 billion pesos, lower than the previous day's 2.24 billion.
"The cut in interest rates was a welcome development but still the levels are relatively high," said Juanis Barredo, analyst at Citisecurities Inc.
The central bank reduced its overnight borrowing rate to 18 percent from 20 percent earlier today while lending rate was lowered to 22 percent from 25 percent.
"The interest rate cut is a positive signal but investors will now be looking at how corporate earnings would fare after the high interest rate regime," said DBS Securities' Trinidad.
Index heavyweights which dragged the main index down were Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, Metropolitan Bank and Manila Electric Co B.
Second and thirdliner issues such as MacroAsia Corp and Republic Resources and Development Corp bucked the trend by posting gains.
In the broad market, there were 73 unchanged issues as against 54 gainers and 52 losers.

"With the correction today, we may be heading lower. People want more concrete stories. The cuts in interest rates are just temporary measures. The central bank has to find the equilibrium point that will be good for the fixed income and the stock market," said Jonathan Ravelas, head of sales at Asian Capital Equities.
Traders have pegged the initial support level at 2,650.
